=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of the Seller update and Disclosure Letter

**Threshold points**
- The Seller's labels ([STANDARD], "FINAL", "cleared by both sides") and its "market" statements are the Seller's own assertions. I have found nothing in the record showing Wattlebridge agreed any of these positions. I have reviewed every item on its merits. Please confirm with the deal lead whether anything was actually settled at principal level.
- The market ranges quoted are unverified and selective. Even if accurate, they would apply only to general warranties, not to title, tax, specific indemnities or fraud.
- The Disclosure Letter is dated as at 22 September 2026. We need a bring-down to Completion.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general warranty claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap, with fundamental, tax, indemnity and fraud claims outside it and capped only at the price (or uncapped for fraud).
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 30–35%, with fall-back room to 25%. The identified exposures (Bluefen at ~30% of revenue, the incident, Ironquay) justify more than 20%, and the cap must apply only to general warranties.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis, and a AUD 250,000 deductible basket (only the excess is recoverable).
- **Buyer wants:** A lower de minimis that aggregates related claims, and a tipping basket (recovery from the first dollar once the threshold is passed). Thresholds should not apply to fundamental, tax, indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at AUD 10,000 and a tipping basket of about 0.5% (~AUD 120,000). A deductible basket combined with a high de minimis erodes recovery for a business with many small data and contract issues.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, and any limitation applies to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months so the buyer sees two audit cycles, and carve-outs stated expressly.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months for general warranties. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default, because it silently shortens every other regime.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Cap at 100% of price, no de minimis or basket, and the longest practicable period (at least the 6-year contract limitation period).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Failure of title means the buyer receives nothing for its AUD 24m, so a 20% cap and an 18-month limit make no sense.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** None offered. Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so no limitation, exclusion or non-reliance clause applies to fraud, dishonest concealment or wilful misconduct, including that of the Seller or the Company's management.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "all Claims of any nature" language and insert the carve-out. The absence of one is a significant gap, not drafting tidiness.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure only against specific warranties, with fair and sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. It must not qualify indemnities or fundamental warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. It would let the Seller disclose away nearly every warranty, including the very matters the letter itself says are unresolved.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete it. If anything survives, limit it to the actual knowledge of named individuals, and exclude indemnities, fundamental matters, tax and fraud. Add an express pro-sandbagging clause.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Combined with SPA-N-006, it would remove recourse for every issue found in diligence, and that is exactly why specific indemnities are needed.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only, and the consent is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter admits no final consent and no evidence that the conditions in cl 11.3 are met.
- **Buyer wants:** A condition precedent to Completion: unconditional written consent (or on terms acceptable to the buyer) under cl 11.2, with the 11.3 conditions satisfied. Add a long-stop date and a buyer termination right.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue, so this is a core value driver. A consent that arrives with unmet conditions must not count as satisfaction.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "following Completion." Disclosure Letter confirms ~AUD 3.2m is unpaid and there is no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** Payout at Completion out of the price under a payout letter, with simultaneous release and discharge of all security (including PPSR and any share charge) and the change-control (cl 8.1) issue resolved.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. This is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal. The debt should reduce the price and be repaid at Completion.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** Treat the bonuses as a transaction cost or debt-like item deducted from the price, plus on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax), or paid by the Seller at or before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. They are triggered by Completion and will land on the Company the buyer owns. Ask the Seller to quantify the on-costs, since the Disclosure Letter is silent on them.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity for any claim relating to ownership, licence or use of the SOW3 materials. Also, as a Completion deliverable, proof of cleared payment of the AUD 180,000 (DD-004 cl 7.3) and a confirmatory IP assignment. Back this with a retention or escrow if either is outstanding.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The Seller admits there is no payment receipt or assignment, and DD-010 is not bank verification, so title to the materials is currently unproven.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity, outside the cap, basket and knowledge qualifier, for investigation, notification, regulatory and third-party costs, supported by a retention. Also a Seller covenant to complete the assessment and cooperate before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation. The letter admits ~1,240 records, no determination on access or scope, and no decision on notification. Check when the Company first became aware, as Privacy Act notifiable data breach assessment timeframes may already be running or missed.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs (AUD 330,000 aggregate).
- **Buyer wants:** The contracts (DD-008/DD-011) reviewed for commitment, termination rights and any prepayment or accrual. Add a covenant against new commitments before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Hold open pending review. Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each look like a single commitment split up, and the Disclosure Letter does not say they are unavoidable. If they are committed and not terminable, seek a price adjustment.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Single regime. Limits apply to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise, and title is treated like a general warranty.
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct categories, each with its own cap, thresholds and period: (1) general warranties, (2) fundamental/title, (3) tax, (4) specific indemnities, (5) fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Restructure cl 12 so limits apply only to category 1 by default, rather than the reverse.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012. The letter itself says this does not mean the Buyer has verified title.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification (ASIC extract, constitution, issue and transfer history, shareholder agreements, PPSR and any share charge, including under the Riverlark security), plus Seller authority approvals and a title warranty as a Completion deliverable.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the register as proof. Complete verification before signing and make clean title a condition.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Settled under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** A separate tax indemnity (or deed) for pre-Completion tax, with a period of at least the tax amendment period plus a buffer (commonly 5–7 years) and no basket or de minimis. IP warranties (ownership, third-party and open-source rights) should sit in an elevated tier.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled." The Seller's own package shows IP is not clean (Ironquay), and putting tax and IP under a 20% cap and 18-month limit leaves long-tail exposure with the buyer.

---

**Suggested next steps**
1. Send a mark-up rejecting the [STANDARD]/"FINAL" labelling and expressly reserving all positions.
2. Request: Bluefen consent status, Riverlark payout letter, Ironquay payment proof and assignment, DD-005 on-cost figures, the Sandbar contracts, and the incident log and forensic report.
3. Build the funds flow with Riverlark (AUD 3.2m), bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs) and any confirmed Sandbar or Ironquay amounts as price deductions or Completion payments.

I can draft the mark-up language or a request list for the Seller if useful.
